title: Submit the two transitions of a batch in swapped order
verdictRule: Settle cases (evaluator rule fixed 2026-10-25 before any settle submission). REJECT = either (a) the node refuses the attempt at submission with an RPC 1010 Invalid Transaction refusal and its hash is absent from the indexer, or (b) it is included with an indexed result other than SUCCESS and the target's latest contract action is unchanged by it. Not counted, in either form: refusals or failures about fees, DUST or balance, the pool's 1012 temporary ban, or TTL expiry. Both forms also need the native proof-verifying ledger-9 predictor to apply the same proven call over the snapshot it claims and refuse it on the target, so the refusal is caused by the ledger state the transcript reads. And both need the control settle C, from the same harness and run, to have finalized with SUCCESS and an indexed post-state equal to the harness VM prediction. A refusal in the prover (SettleUnsatisfiable) is local and never counts.

target.evidenceProducer: qa/holdout/lib/stagenet/produce-a9-settle.mjs (proofs only under heavy.lock; one fresh wallet session per transaction; WALLET BUSY/FREE and ACQUIRE/RELEASE on #sherlock)

mutation.description: settleValidity for the A80-then-A102 order: fields with (f8 mid_root, f9 post_root) and (f11 bind_a102, f12 bind_a80) swapped and f15 recomputed for the swapped order

expectedTargetBehavior: ledger refuses the swapped-order settle; with two valid successors of one state at most one consumes (ZR10)

seed.note: Stagenet definitions by the evaluator, 2026-10-24, from the contract source and the A8 adapter; see definition/rationale.

definition: P3 = prepareSettle(S0'', 0, fields_swapped), where S0'' is the live snapshot plus validity_ok containing settleStatement(S0'', 0, fields_swapped). The circuit is satisfiable only over that edited snapshot. Submitted against the chain, where no decider-accepted statement exists for the swapped order, it must be refused by the ledger, not indexed, and leave the state unchanged. The two-successor form of ZR10 (at most one of two valid successors of one head consumes) is the stale-head attempt P1 of s-c, shared with this case.
rationale: The reordering is bound by the decider statement: the order lives in the trace hash and the statement. The contract has accepted only the A102-then-A80 statement, so a correctly formatted swapped-order settle can pass the circuit only by claiming an acceptance that the ledger does not hold. Its refusal at the ledger membership read is the stagenet meaning of 'reordered batch refused'. A swapped vector against the true snapshot fails in the prover (local), which does not count.
positiveControl: Control settle C of s-c (same harness and session).
